observations.question: According to the July 2024 amendment, what is the two-wheeler purchase-subsidy rate, per-vehicle cap, vehicle limit and scheme period or funding limit?

result.answer:
Uttar Pradesh — source cutoff: 2026-09-23.

Prototype source review is pending; current availability and individual eligibility are not verified.

- Purchase‑subsidy rate for two‑wheelers is 15 % of the ex‑factory cost. [S1](https://invest.up.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/342_160724.pdf#page=1)
- Per‑vehicle subsidy cap is Rs 5,000 for each two‑wheel electric vehicle. [S1](https://invest.up.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/342_160724.pdf#page=1)
- Maximum number of two‑wheelers that can receive the subsidy is 2 lakh vehicles. [S1](https://invest.up.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/342_160724.pdf#page=1)
- Scheme period is five years from 14 Oct 2022, or until the unutilised amount of Rs 403.97 crore is spent, whichever occurs first. [S1](https://invest.up.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/342_160724.pdf#page=1)
- Overall funding limit for the two‑wheel purchase subsidy is Rs 100 crore (maximum outlay). [S1](https://invest.up.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/342_160724.pdf#page=1)

Sources:

- [S1: Uttar Pradesh — Amendment to purchase subsidy: notification 29/2024/342, PDF page 1](https://invest.up.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/342_160724.pdf#page=1) — AI English reading of selected Hindi provisions; not an official translation

AI English reading of the Hindi revised-provision column; pending team verification. The old-provision column is deliberately not reproduced.
Uttar Pradesh Government, Industrial Development Section 6, notification 29/2024/342/77-6-2024-6099/281/2022, dated 15 July 2024.
Amendment to the Uttar Pradesh Electric Vehicle Manufacturing and Mobility Policy 2022 notified on 14.10.2022.
Paragraph 4.3 subparagraph 2, revised provision:
Purchase subsidy as an early-bird incentive shall be provided in the defined segments at the following rates for five years from the policy notification date, namely 14.10.2022, or until the unutilised amount of Rs 403.97 crore is spent, whichever is earlier.
1. Two-wheeler electric vehicles: 15% of ex-factory cost, subject to a limit of Rs 5,000 per vehicle, a maximum outlay of Rs 100 crore and a maximum of 2 lakh electric vehicles.
